entries.title: 3:12 AM
entries.text:
Couldn't sleep, so I watched one of those videos. "HOW TO LUCID DREAM TONIGHT! (100% WORKING)." The guy was so sure of himself it was almost funny.

I wrote his rules down anyway. Five of them. Mirrors, scary thoughts, telling people, asking about the real world, pushing the walls around.

The towel is still over the mirror. I don't remember when I put it there.

entries.title: The Summer Dream
entries.text:
It worked. It actually worked.

A city in the middle of summer, warm stone, a fountain, kids with kites. I thought of ice cream and it was in my hand. Cold. Real.

The people were kind. Strange, a little. Nobody remembered it ever raining. The pigeons stopped when I asked the old man the wrong question.

There was a man at the end of the street. I don't think he was a man.

When I tried to wake up, the floor wasn't there anymore.

entries.title: The Yellow Rooms
entries.text:
Yellow walls. Wet carpet. A hum that never stops, coming from the lights, or the walls, or the inside of my head.

The rooms moved when I wasn't looking. Not much. A wall where there wasn't a wall. A chair I'd already passed, waiting for me again. A picture of the summer street, with something small and black standing in it.

My notebook had a sixth rule in it. My handwriting. I didn't write it.

I found the door by following the hum.

entries.title: The Deep End
entries.text:
A swimming pool at night, lit from under the water. The kind of quiet that has a sound.

The deep end had no bottom. The water only went down while I watched it. As if it needed a witness.

Under it, there was the sea. All of it. Cliffs going down forever, and things moving in the dark that were only lights until they weren't.

I could breathe. I shouldn't have been able to.

Something took hold of my ankles.

entries.title: THE DEEP
entries.text:
The bottom of the sea is very quiet.

I held a light I had imagined and followed stones that glowed, because something enormous was circling above me, waiting for me to step wrong.

It came for me at the cliff. It didn't fit through the opening. I keep thinking about that: that the dream had rules even for it.

There was a door at the back of the cave, full of light.

I don't know what's on the other side of it yet.

After the cave there was more. A drowned building with corridors too narrow to turn in. A room with three doors that all opened into itself. A room with none. A door I could only go through backwards, without looking.

Four trenches in a cross, and four lights across them. I lit them. Something far below turned toward every one.

It was waiting at the station. It had been waiting the whole time.

entries.title: COMPRESSION
entries.text:
A basement under a building I've never lived in. Every corridor a little narrower than the last, every ceiling a little lower. The way I came in turned into wall while my back was turned.

There was a room whose walls only moved when I wasn't looking at them, so I walked it looking left, then right, then left, like a child crossing a road. There was something breathing in the vent behind me. Not my breathing. I checked.

And the drying room. Sheets on lines, and shapes under three of them, standing very still. They were closer every time I looked back. I didn't look back much.

The elevator said MAX 1 PERSON. On the way up it got smaller.

The lift went up into a building that doesn't fit inside itself. A flat with a park bench in it. A yellow hallway, humming, longer than the street outside. A child's room, and him, in the corner.

The stairs only went down if I climbed down. Floor seven. Then the building came down behind me, all of it, a step behind me the whole way. I don't know how I outran it. I don't think I did.

entries.title: ABOVE
entries.text:
The elevator opened onto a roof above the clouds. Towers all around, going down into the fog further than towers go.

I walked out along a plank over nothing to get a key, because there was a key at the end of it. I crossed a steel beam on my hands and knees when the wind came. When I looked back the beam wasn't there anymore.

Someone fell past, far away. No sound until they were already gone. I don't think it was anyone. I think it was supposed to be me.

There was a red light at the top of the mast. It was warm.

A lift that went sideways through floors that don't exist. Stairs in the open air that were only there when I got close. A crane, a girder, a glass bridge that cracked under me.

The mast. The light at the top. When I touched it, the platform took itself apart and built a path, piece by piece, up into the sky. There was a door at the end of it, just standing there.

I went through. I think I'm still going through.
